Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-rays demonstrate a marked shift of the mediastinum and cardiac silhouette into the right hemithorax following right-sided surgery, with an abnormal cardiac contour and hyperlucent left lung field. This displacement of the heart into the empty pleural space is characteristic of right-sided cardiac herniation, a known complication after extrapleural pneumonectomy or extensive pleural resection that causes acute hemodynamic compromise due to torsion of the great vessels.
